scope: NeverC i386 Linux source ABI and native BOUND interfaces, Clang indirect varargs repair, and actual NeverD export interoperation

source_identity.export_provenance: x86-legacy-bound-2026-11-04.json qualification.final_integration; preserved integration-native and integration-r6 exports

contract.frontend: Linux ELF i386/i486/i586/i686, ILP32, x87 long double in 12-byte storage, correct legacy CPU defaults and shared x86 builtins. Emit LLVM IR or bitcode using --target=i386-unknown-linux-gnu.
contract.abi: X86/SysV32 owns scalar and aggregate classification, sret, byval, alignment, x87, complex, vectors, wide _BitInt, regparm and stdcall. Variadic extraction reuses its argument classifier; wide scalars exhaust the register bank before their indirect pointer is classified.
contract.bound: Four source builtins lower to effectful native LLVM BOUND calls. Long-mode use and invalid address/prefix constants fail explicitly; unused and repeated calls retain ordering and faults.
contract.clang_repair: X86_32ABIInfo::EmitVAArg now distinguishes indirect pointer slots from direct byval stack images. Large _BitInt values advance va_list by pointer width and load through the slot, preserving natural pointee alignment.
contract.capabilities: The builtin route advertises source=true, assembly=false, object=false, MC decode=false. Ordinary i386 -c/-S are rejected because the embedded backend is still pruned. Existing machine fixtures filter by object capability.

qualification.host: Intel Core i9-13900H; CPU 2 P core and CPU 12 E core; Linux ELF32 multilib and modify_ldt available

abi.meaning: 8 O0/O2 caller/callee combinations per core: Clang/Clang, NeverC/Clang, Clang/NeverC, NeverC/NeverC. NeverC uses full LLVM for object lowering. Includes bitcode verification, va_copy, 65/97-bit values, callee cleanup, register exhaustion and callback transport.

bound.meaning: Direct LLVM and actual NeverC source, O0/O2 on both cores. Independent original bytes witness signed inclusive bounds, full input return, FS/address wrapping, access/fault ordering and unused/repeated calls.

neverd_exports.meaning: Native-SDK exports on CPU 2 and pinned-r6 exports on CPU 12, each at O0/O2. Each run compiles all 336 HighC/LLVMC files, executes 72 source cases plus 12 original exported ELF objects, verifies IR and machine instructions, forbids BOUND inline-asm fallback and checks 336 native BOUND instructions.

diagnostics.controls: All wrong-index and truncated-return controls retain native BOUND or the real call graph and fail with exit 1. Missing machine backend, unsupported platforms/fastcall, invalid controls and long-mode BOUND are rejected.

remaining_boundaries: NeverC embedded i386 machine selection, frame/calling-convention lowering, MC, linker and packaged runtime/sysroot remain unavailable. The full LLVM fork still supplies object code.
NeverC other 32-bit operating systems, fastcall/vectorcall/regcall, code16 frontend, -m32 driver shorthand and x64-only builtin families are not enabled by this batch.

This source ABI evidence does not implement NeverD general i386 original-state source dispatch, task/VM86 transitions, unimplemented software SMM/SGX events, CET/FRED or multicore/device environments.
The single skipped plugin test concerns case-alias filesystem detection. No blanket all-instruction or all-platform completion claim is made.
